metrics.question: how long should i roast a whole chicken
metrics.answer: The sources don't give a cooking time for a whole chicken. Roasting is generally done at temperatures of at least 150 °C (300 °F) using indirect, diffused heat, which suits slower cooking of a large whole piece [1]. Roast a whole chicken at around 190 °C (375 °F) until the thickest part of the thigh reaches 74 °C (165 °F).

metrics.question: how long should i roast a whole chicken
metrics.answer: The sources don't give a specific cooking time for a whole chicken. Roasting is generally done at temperatures of at least 150 °C (300 °F) using indirect, diffused heat in an oven, which suits larger whole pieces of meat [1]. As a general guide, a whole chicken typically takes roughly 1.5 to 2 hours at around 180 °C (350 °F), checking that the thickest part of the thigh reaches 74 °C (165 °F).
